title: Longest Subarray With Equal 0s and 1s
statement:
You are given a binary array `a` of length `n` (every element is `0` or `1`). Find the **longest contiguous subarray that contains the same number of `0`s and `1`s**.

Report it by the indices of its first and last element (0-indexed, both inclusive), so its length is `end - start + 1`. If several subarrays share the maximum length, report the one with the **smallest start index**. If no subarray has equal counts of `0`s and `1`s, report `-1`.

**Follow-up:** If you are only asked for the length of the longest such subarray, can you drop anything from your solution? The related interview question also asks to simulate a fair six-sided die roll without any built-in random function; that part is a discussion item and is not tested here.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers, each `0` or `1`.
outputFormat: Print two integers `start end` separated by a space, or `-1` if no subarray has an equal number of `0`s and `1`s.

examples.explanation: The whole array has three 0s and three 1s, so the longest subarray runs from index 0 to index 5.
Both [1,0,0,1] (indices 0 to 3) and [0,0,1,1] (indices 1 to 4) are balanced and have length 4. The tie goes to the smaller start index, 0.
Every subarray contains only 1s, so none has an equal number of 0s and 1s.

hints: Checking every pair of endpoints is O(n^2). Think of each 0 as -1 and each 1 as +1: a balanced subarray is one whose values sum to 0.
With running prefix sums, a subarray (i, j] sums to 0 exactly when the prefix sums at i and j are equal.

Store the first index at which each prefix sum appears. For each j, the longest balanced subarray ending at j starts right after that first index. Update the answer only for strictly longer lengths to get the smallest start on ties.
